On his daughter Anna's death act he is «PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — WITHOUT «fu» or «defunto». So he was alive on 23 August 1820, a contadino, living on strada Camellara, fourteen years before his own death act of 1 October 1834. This is an independent civil sighting of the ancestor between his marriage and his death.

«e di CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — named without «fu» on her daughter Anna's death act, so alive in August 1820 and living on strada Camellara. Until now the only record naming her at all was her own Latin burial entry of 1843.

«sono comparsi PASQUALE FALCO, di anni cinquantacinque, di professione COLONO, regnicolo, domiciliato in questo comune strada Camellara, ZIO DEL DEFUNTO, e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, ZIO DEL DEFUNTO» — atto 8. THE WORD IS «ZIO», NOT «VICINO», AND THIS ARCHIVE READ IT WRONG. Re-read 16 Sep 2026 at full magnification: the word before «del defunto» is three letters, written twice, and it is not the six-letter «vicino» the same clerk writes on the 1823 and 1825 acts of this same household — those two acts are the control, and they are in this file to be checked against. So the register states in 1824 that the dead child's mother MARIA FALCO is kin to these two men, four years before the 1828 act on which this archive had rested that conclusion. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE. Read strictly, «zio del defunto» makes Maria Falco a SISTER of Pasquale (bapt. 24 October 1767) and of Giuseppe — and therefore a daughter of MATTEO FALCO and FRANCESCA CRISCI. Her own stated age forbids it: twenty-five in June 1824, born about 1799, when Francesca Crisci was bearing children by 1767. Either that age is one of this register's inventions — and this archive holds the same clerk making Giuseppe Falco forty and forty-five four days apart — or «zio» is doing the loose collateral work that «parente» does in 1828. THE WORD IS RECORDED AND THE PEDIGREE IS REFUSED. THE ONLY RECORD IN WHICH PASQUALE FALCO ACTS FOR HIMSELF, and the only document in this archive written in his own hand: the act closes «segnato da noi e da uno de' dichiaranti, avendo l'altro cioè GIUSEPPE FALCO dichiarato di non sapere scrivere per non averlo mai imparato», and beneath it, in a slow upright hand quite unlike the clerk's, stands the signature «PASCALE FALCO» — the Neapolitan form, without the qu, the way he said his own name. His brother could not sign. He is fifty-five here, one year out against his baptism of 24 October 1767 — ordinary — and his trade is COLONO, a tenant farmer, where his death act of 1834 calls him contadino.

«è morta nella sua propria casa MARIA FALCO d'anni TRENTADUE, moglie di ALFONSO DIGLIO, nata in Arienzo, di professione Contadina, domiciliata ivi, FIGLIA DI PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi, E DI CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — atto 22. FALCO ANGELANDREA | Arienzo | FALCO VINCENZO, e CRISCI ANDREANA» ed «CIMMINO MARIA | Arienzo | CIMMINO ALESSANDRO, e SOLLI [ROSA]», the church date given as 24 MARZO [1847]. When Angelandrea's birth act of 12 September 1826 was published, it was DELIBERATELY NOT JOINED to «the ANGELO Falco who married Maria Cimmino in 1847 or the ANDREA Falco who married Maria Carmela», because the household held all three names and each of the other two was known only from a parish marriage act. THE CIVIL INDEX SETTLES ONE HALF: the man who married MARIA CIMMINO, daughter of Alessandro and Rosa Solli, is written ANGELANDREA — the exact name of the 1826 birth act — so ANGELO of the parish act and ANGELANDREA of the birth act are ONE MAN, married at TWENTY. The ANDREA who married Maria Carmela, daughter of Onofrio and Angela Imbimbo, REMAINS A SEPARATE SON and is still not joined to anything. DATE DISCREPANCY RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED: this tavola gives the church wedding as 24 March 1847 and the parish record held here gives 17 April 1847 — the same kind of civil-versus-parish disagreement already documented for Raffaele Falco's marriage of 1844

members.evidence: THE CIVIL ACT BEHIND A BAPTISM THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD — not a new child. Act 133: «è comparso VINCENZO FALCO, di anni VENTISEI, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo comune, STRADA CAMELLARA … ad ore dieci è nato nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante e da ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legitima d'Anni VENTIDUE, un MASCHIO … a cui si è dato il nome di LUIGI». The parish entry gave only «Dec 1819» and «nominatus est Aloysius»; this gives the day, the hour, the street and both parents' ages.

«di anni VENTISEI» — twenty-six. He was given as TWENTY-SEVEN on 10 May 1818, nineteen months earlier: HE GETS YOUNGER BY A YEAR WHILE NINETEEN MONTHS PASS. His baptism of 1 February 1792 makes him twenty-seven here, so both civil figures are wrong and the register is the reason the archive dates him from the font instead.

«d'Anni VENTIDUE» — twenty-two, so b. c.1797. This is the Andreana Crisci who married Vincenzo Falco in December 1814, on his own street and in his own house; she is not the other Andreana Crisci this archive keeps separate.

«*MARITO DI **CAROLINA CIMMINO***» — Luigi Falco's widow, and a person this archive did not know existed. Nothing else about her is established: no marriage act, no parents, no age. **The Arienzo civil marriage record is complete 1809–1858 and holds no Falco–Cimmino wedding**, so they married after 1858 or not at Arienzo.

GENERATION THREE, ALIVE AT SEVENTY-TWO — twenty years later than any sighting this archive had. «*figlio di **VINCENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **alla Camellara***», with **no «fu» and no «defunto»**. **THE FORM MARKS THE DEAD AND THIS REGISTER USES IT**: on the same opening, act 41 gives «*figlio di **fu** Nicola … e della **fu** Colomba Capezzo*», act 43 «*figlia del **fu** Giuseppe … e della **fu** Cecilia Silvestri*», act 45 «*figlia del **fu** Don Stefano … e della **fu** Donna Faustina Cimmino*», act 49 «*figlio del **fu** Filippo … e della **fu** Lucrezia Varrecchia*». Four dead parents marked on one sheet, and these two not. His baptism of 1 February 1792 makes him seventy-two.
«*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***» — alive, unmarked, on the same evidence as her husband. Her latest previous sighting was her son Raffaele's marriage act of 7 March 1844.

A CHILD OF GENERATION THREE THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **STANISLAO FALCO**, di anni **VENTIQUATTRO**, nato in **ARIENZO**, di professione **PASTORE**, domiciliato in Arienzo, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in Arienzo, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata ivi; e **FILOMENA DI LUCIA**, di anni ventitré, nata in Arienzo, figlia di fu [?] di Lucia, **muratore**, e di **MARTA di NIZZO***». Church celebration **23 September 1861**, parish of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**. **A PASTORE — a shepherd — in a house of contadini.** Twenty-four in September 1861 gives **b. c.1837**, which would make Andreana Crisci about forty at his birth: late, but this register's ages are good to about three years and no better, and she was bearing children into 1828 on the archive's own reckoning.

ALIVE AT SIXTY-NINE, three years before the other sighting. «*figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **Arienzo***» — **no «fu», no «defunto»**, in an act that marks the bride's father dead in the very next clause («*figlia di **fu** [?] di Lucia*»).

«*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***» — alive, unmarked, on the same evidence. This is the Andreana Crisci who married Vincenzo Falco in December 1814, not the other woman of the name this archive keeps separate.

Stanislao Falco's bride: **twenty-three**, born Arienzo, so b. c.1838. **Her parents are LUIGI DI LUCIA, *muratore*, and MARTA DI NIZZO** — the father's forename is illegible on the marriage act itself and comes from the **NOTIFICAZIONI register bound into the same volume**, which gives the same couple in a clerk's cleaner hand: «*matrimonio tra **STANISLAO FALCO** figlio di **VINCENZO** e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, e **FILOMENA DI LUCIA** figlia di **LUIGI** e di **MARTA DI NIZZO***». Her father was already dead at the wedding.

THE REGISTER ACT BEHIND THE INDEX ENTRY. Act 14: «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANDREA FALCO maggiore**, di anni **VENTIQUATTRO**, nato in **Arienzo**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato ivi, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, di professione **FILATRICE**, domiciliata ivi; e **MARIA CARMELA BUONO maggiore**, di anni ventiquattro, di professione filatrice, nata in Arienzo, domiciliata in **strada Porta di Sopra***». Church **24 May 1846** at Sant'Andrea, which is the date the index gave. Witnesses Agostino di Giglio and **Gennaro Laudato**. **TWENTY-FOUR IN MAY 1846 GIVES b. c.1822** — four years before Angelandrea, and the two are separate men on the ages alone.

**«MINORE» — AND THAT ONE WORD CONFIRMS HIS BIRTH ACT.** Act on img4r: «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **ANGELANDREA FALCO MINORE**, di anni **venti[…]**, nato in Arienzo, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **strada Camellara**, figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, **colono**, e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, **filatrice** … e **MARIA CIMMINO maggiore** … nata in Arienzo, domiciliata in **strada Capodiconca**, figlia di **ALESSANDRO CIMMINO**, contadino*». Church **29 March 1847** at Sant'Andrea. Witnesses **Gennaro Laudato** and Francesco de Angelis. **MAJORITY WAS TWENTY-ONE**, so «minore» puts him under it — and his birth act of **12 September 1826** makes him twenty years and six months. The numeral itself carries a flourish and is not read beyond «venti[…]»; **the word «minore» is what bounds him, and it is unambiguous.** **A DATE CONFLICT, RECORDED NOT RESOLVED:** this archive also holds «Angelo Falco … m. Maria Cimmino» on **17 April 1847** from a parish ark — the same bride, three weeks later. Both are kept.

A SIGHTING IN THE 1844–1861 GAP. «*figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO**, di professione **COLONO**, domiciliato ivi*» — no «fu», in an act whose own next clause marks the bride's father when he is dead. Named the same way again on 29 March 1847.

**HER TRADE, FOR THE FIRST TIME: FILATRICE — a spinner.** «*e di **ANDREANA CRISCI**, di professione **filatrice**, domiciliata ivi*». Alive and unmarked, and given the same way again on 29 March 1847. This archive had her age five times and her occupation never.

Andrea Falco's bride: twenty-four, **filatrice**, born Arienzo, of **strada Porta di Sopra**, daughter of **ONOFRIO BUONO** and **ANGELA IMBIMBO** — the parents from the index, now with her own age, trade and street.

Josephum Falco filium Matthei, e Franciscae Crisci — son of Matteo — and in June 1818 he declares a daughter's birth as a contadino of STRADA CAMELLARA, aged 36, which puts his own birth about 1782 and places a documented son of Matteo Falco on the family's street.

members.evidence: «e di Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentadue, massaro di campagna, domiciliato ugualmente nel luogo indicato» — declaring the death of Crescenzo Rivetti alongside Gioacchino Falco, the two of them «parenti del defunto». PLACED HERE WITH RESERVATION: the street matches this household, but the age does not. This man is 32 in December 1816; the Giuseppe of strada Camellara is 36 in June 1818, which would make him 34 here. The trade differs too — massaro di campagna against contadino. It may be the same man loosely aged, or a third Giuseppe.

«Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentasette, di professione massaro di campagna, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara» — twice in five days: on 24 October for a neighbour, Marianna Petrillo, and on 28 October for Vincenzo Falco's infant son Raffaele, where he and Sabato Vassallo are called «PARENTI». Vincenzo is a grandson of Matteo; Giuseppe is a documented son of Matteo, which would make him Vincenzo's uncle — and the register's own word for the relationship is kin. Aged 37 here, so born about 1780.

«e di Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentasei, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara» — declaring the death of a neighbour, Emanuela d'Onofrio, with Domenico Balletta, 40, sartore, of the same street. THIS IS THE SIGHTING THAT TIES THE OTHERS TOGETHER: one month later, on 7 June 1818, the birth act of his daughter Maddalena gives him as thirty-six, contadino, of strada Camellara, husband of Antonia di Guida. Same age, same trade, same street, four weeks apart — one man, not two. Balletta is his neighbour in October 1817 as well.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantatre, di professione Contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato strada Camellara» — THE FIRST CIVIL RECORD TO STATE HIS PARENTAGE OUTRIGHT. The clerk adds «fu Matteo» to tell him from the other Giuseppe Falco of the town, and in doing so confirms from the civil series what the archive previously had only from the parish books: this Giuseppe is a son of the late Matteo Falco. Forty-three here, so born about 1780 — which agrees with the thirty-seven he gives in October 1817. He declares with Cesare Giglio, 50, of the same street, at the death of Maria Crisci, three years old, daughter of Marcello Crisci and Maria Rosa Mauro.

«sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantadue, di professione Contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Sant'Andrea, vicino della defunta» — atto 39, the SECOND «fu Matteo» sighting in two days, at the death of Antonia Cossi, nine months old, daughter of Francesco Cossi and a MARIA FALCO. TWO CAUTIONS. He is forty-two here and forty-three the day before, from the same clerk — a plain measure of how loosely these ages are kept. And he is given here on STRADA SANT'ANDREA where the day before he is on strada Camellara: in this form a declarant described as «vicino» is recorded at the street of the house where the death happened, so a declarant's street is NOT reliable evidence of where he himself lived. RE-READ 16 Sep 2026: the second declarant, not recorded here before, is ANIELLO DIGLIO, 46, contadino, «domiciliato ivi strada Sant'Andrea, vicino della defunta». He stands with a Falco over this household's dead again in April 1825.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, ZIO DEL DEFUNTO» — CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive read «vicino del defunto». The word is ZIO, and it is written twice on this act, once for each brother. Declaring beside his brother PASQUALE FALCO: the only act found so far in which the two appear together, and the first to give Giuseppe's trade as colono rather than contadino. Forty-two here, so born about 1782. AND HE COULD NOT WRITE: the act closes by naming him as the declarant who «dichiarato di non sapere scrivere per non averlo mai imparato», while Pasquale signs. What the word «zio» does and does not establish about MARIA FALCO is set out on Pasquale's row for this same act; it is recorded and not resolved.

«sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione MASSARO, regnicolo, domiciliato in strada Camellara, vicino della defunta, ed ANIELLO DIGLIO, di anni quarantasei, contadino» — a seventh sighting, and THE THIRD TIME HE STANDS FOR THE SAME HOUSE. Francesco Cossi and Maria Falco lost Antonia in June 1823, Giuseppe in March 1824 and Giuseppa here in April 1825, and Giuseppe Falco declared every one. CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive wrote here that the register called him «vicino» each time and never stated a relationship. THE MIDDLE ACT OF THE THREE CALLS HIM «ZIO DEL DEFUNTO». So the register does state a relationship, and this reading — a pattern of appearances but no statement of kinship — was built on a misread word. What stands is that he is «vicino della defunta» on THIS act and on the 1823 act, and «zio» in 1824 and «parente» in 1828: the clerk wrote whichever the declarant offered, and a man could be both the neighbour and the uncle on one street. His trade drifts again: contadino in 1823, colono in 1824, MASSARO here; and his age goes backwards, forty here against forty-two the year before.

«è morta nella sua propria casa MADDALENA FALCO, d'anni SETTE, nata in Arienzo, di professione Contadina, figlia di GIUSEPPE FALCO, di professione Contadino, e di ANTONIA DI GUIDA» — atto 30. THIS CLOSES A LIFE THE ARCHIVE HAD ONLY OPENED: her civil birth act of 7 June 1818 records her born on strada Camellara to Giuseppe, thirty-six, and Antonia, and she died a week short of her seventh birthday. A documented grandchild of Matteo Falco and Francesca Crisci, and a first cousin of Vincenzo Falco's children. Declared by CESARE COSSI, 30, and FRANCESCO COSSI, 34, both of strada Camellara — and Francesco Cossi is very likely the husband of the Maria Falco for whose three dead children Giuseppe Falco had stood in 1823, 1824 and 1825. The two houses declare for each other.

«è morto nella sua propria casa CLEMENTE FALCO, di mesi QUINDICI, nato in Arienzo, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO, di professione contadino, e di ANTONIA DI GUIDA» — born about March 1824, a child of this house the archive did not have. HE DIED NINETEEN DAYS AFTER HIS SISTER MADDALENA, who was seven. Declared by MARCELLO COSSI, 35, and ANIELLO DIGLIO, 50, both of strada Camellara — Diglio is the same neighbour who stood with Giuseppe in April, when he was given as forty-six.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTASEI, di professione MASSARO, regnicolo, domiciliato in strada Camellara, vicino del Defunto» — declaring atto 56, the death of Giuseppe Cossi, two, son of Gaspare Cossi and Maria Sposito. Aged 46, so born about 1780; he was 37 and «massaro di campagna» on the same street in October 1817.

Declaring atto 73 TOGETHER WITH CARLANTONIO MORGILLO, 46, contadino, of the same street — the FIRST ACT IN THE WHOLE ARIENZO SERIES in which a Falco and a Morgillo stand side by side. Both are entered as «vicini», so it is not a kinship statement; it is the earliest evidence that the two houses the line would later join were already neighbours.

«Sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in strada Camellara, vicino del Defunto» — declaring atto 30, the death of Giuseppe Cossi, aged one, son of Francesco Cossi. THE FOURTH CHILD OF THAT HOUSEHOLD he has declared (1823, 1824, 1825, 1827); the register calls him «vicino» every time and never «parente». NOTE THE AGE: 37 in 1817, 40 in 1825, 46 twice in 1826, 40 here — and the trade slides from massaro di campagna to massaro to colono. Either the clerks guessed or there are two Giuseppe Falco on that street.

«Sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni CINQUANTASEI, di professione POSSIDENTE, domiciliato in strada Camellara, PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA» — atto 54, on the death of Mariantonia Cossi, seven months, daughter of Francesco Cossi and Maria Falco. THE FIFTH CHILD OF THAT HOUSE HE HAS DECLARED, and the FIRST TIME THE REGISTER CALLS HIM PARENTE rather than vicino. The kinship between Maria Falco and this Giuseppe Falco is now stated by the record; the degree is not. Caution: he is 56 and a possidente here, against 40 and a colono eighteen months earlier — either the clerks guessed, or there are two Giuseppe Falco on that street.

AN EIGHTH CHILD, and the clearest necronym in this household. The 1827 tavola reads «52. Falco Maddalena | Falco Giuseppe, e Guida d'Antonia | A dì 4 Maggio 1827». THE FIRST MADDALENA DIED ON 31 MAY 1825, aged seven, on strada Camellara; this one was born TWENTY-THREE MONTHS LATER and given her name. From the tavola, which is contemporaneous and in the registrar's hand; the act itself (atto 52) has not been read

members.evidence: HIS BIRTH DATE, FOUND AT LAST — he was held by his marriages alone. Civil act 99, folio 239: «è comparso GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo comune, STRADA CAMELLARA … ad ore cinque è nato nella sua propria casa da lui dichiarante, e da ANTONIA DI GUIDA sua moglie legitima d'anni TRENTUNO, un MASCHIO». THE GIVEN NAME DID NOT RESOLVE IN THE CIVIL HAND at the leaf's maximum resolution. It is supplied by the PARISH page, which was already harvested into this repository and never parsed: `3Q9M-CSD3-13CH-7`, an October 1819 baptism «et Josepho Falco et Anto[nia] di [Guida] Conjugibus», margin «Cresantios» = CRESCENTIUS. Two independent sources, same parents, same month. Graded PROBABLE on the civil act and PROVEN on the join.

Aged FORTY, contadino. He was given as THIRTY-SIX on 7 June 1818, sixteen months earlier — four years of ageing in sixteen months, from one clerk's desk. A fresh instance of the stated-age problem, in the household that supplies most of them.
«d'anni TRENTUNO» — thirty-one, so b. c.1788. This archive has already established that the civil clerks' age for her is about five years out; the figure is recorded, not believed.

THE CIVIL ACT BEHIND THE CHURCH DATE, AND IT DATES HIS BIRTH. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **CRESCENZO FALCO maggiore di anni VENTICINQUE nato in ARIENZO**, di professione **colono**, domiciliato **IVI strada Sant'Andrea**, figlio di **GIUSEPPE FALCO** di professione simile domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** di professione contadina domiciliata **ivi***» — TRANSCRIPTION CORRECTED 16 Sep 2026: this archive wrote «domiciliato **in** strada Sant'Andrea» and the act reads «domiciliato **ivi** strada Sant'Andrea». The dropped word matters, because «ivi» in these forms means THE COMUNE and not the street — the bride in this very act is «domiciliata **ivi strada Cappuccini**», one word and two streets. So GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA are recorded here as domiciled AT ARIENZO, and THE ACT DOES NOT GIVE THEIR STREET. Anything this archive concluded about the household leaving strada Camellara rests on a word that was never there — bride **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, 23, contadina, of strada Cappuccini, «*figlia di **GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO** … e di **MARIA FELICIA SANZONE** … **defunta***». The INDICAZIONE records the church celebration: **3 February 1845**, parish of **Sant'Andrea Apostolo**, witnesses **Luigi Verdicchio** and **Nunzio Rivetti**. TWENTY-FIVE ON 2 FEBRUARY 1845 puts his birth between 3 February 1819 and 2 February 1820 — and his civil birth act is 11 October 1819.

Given with a trade and a domicile and NOT marked «defunto» — in an act that marks BOTH of the bride's parents dead in the same sentence. He was already known alive in November 1849 from his son the deacon's death act; this is an independent sighting on a form that states death explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

HER LATEST DATED SIGHTING BY TWENTY-FIVE YEARS. This archive held her on one dated document — her son Crescenzo's birth act of 11 October 1819. Here she is «*di professione contadina domiciliata ivi*», alive, in an act that writes «DEFUNTO» and «DEFUNTA» for the bride's father and mother. HER DEATH HAS BEEN HUNTED THROUGH THE PARISH REGISTER AND NOT FOUND; the window now opens on 2 February 1845 instead of October 1819.

Crescenzo Falco's bride: twenty-three, contadina, born in Arienzo, and an orphan — «*figlia di GENNARO MORGILLO defunto, di professione colono … e di MARIA FELICIA SANZONE, di professione contadina … defunta*». The church act carries a dispensation «*super quarto gradu consanguinitatis*», so she and Crescenzo were third cousins.

A CONFLICT, PUBLISHED AS ONE. The 1832 death index reads «14. MORGILLO RAFFAELA | Arienzo | contadina | MORGILLO CARLANTONIO, e FALCO ROSA | A 9 MARZO 1832». This archive already holds, from the act, «RAFFAELE MORGILLO, 22, CONTADINO, figlio di Carlantonio Morgillo», died 9 MAY 1832. SAME DAY OF THE MONTH, DIFFERENT MONTH, DIFFERENT ENDING, DIFFERENT SEX. Either this couple lost two children nine weeks apart, or one record has been read two ways — «Marzo» and «Maggio» begin alike, and so do «Raffaela» and «Raffaele». A NEW DAUGHTER for the OTHER Giuseppe Falco, found by reading the 1823 birth register end to end. «…nata da GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTOTTO … nel giorno TRENTA del mese di MARZO … alle ore DIECI … il nome di PASQUA». Her mother's age agrees with this household's other act to within a year — thirty-two in 1816, thirty-eight in 1823. THE MARGIN RECORDS HER MARRIAGE: «A 30 Dic. 1880 l'uff. dello stato civile d'Arienzo … PASQUA FALCO con PASQUALE CARFORA», certified Caserta 27 Aug 1881. SHE IS NOT JOINED TO GIOVANNA ARRICALE'S MOTHER — but she is the ONLY Pasqua born at Arienzo in the whole window Giovanna's act implies: 1822 and 1823 were both read end to end, 239 acts, and 1822 holds no Pasqua at all. Joining them would marry the Camellara Falco to the strada Costa Falco on a forename and an age the clerks are known to have guessed by up to five years. See the corrections page

members.evidence: A NECRONYM, THREE DAYS AFTER A DOUBLE BURIAL. Act 33, folio 206: «è comparso GIUSEPPE FALCO … di professione MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA, domiciliato in detto comune, STRADA CAMELLARA … ad ore sette e mezza è nato … e da GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA sua moglie legitima … un MASCHIO … a cui si è dato il nome di DOMENICO CLEMENTE». THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD THAT THIS COUPLE BURIED TWO CHILDREN ON 15 MARCH 1819 — Domenico, aged two years and four months, and his sister Rosaria eleven hours later. Three days after, a son was born and given the dead boy's name.

FROM THE MARGIN OF HIS OWN BIRTH ACT, not from any marriage register: «*Con atto **6 agosto 1856** at[to] **21** in **S[?] …a Vico** il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI** [di] **Gaspare**(?)*». **THE COMUNE IS NOT ESTABLISHED.** At five times magnification the place reads «*S[?]basia a Vico*» and resolves no further. **SANTA MARIA A VICO IS THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE AND IS EXCLUDED BY ITS OWN REGISTER**: `an_ua55736`, *Matrimoni* 1856, **act 21 is Don Domenico de Lucia, 29, of San Felice, promised 14 June 1856** — no Falco, and no act of 6 August (act 31 is 3 August, act 32 is 9 August). **What is certain is the annotation itself**: a Falco of this house married a DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI on 6 August 1856, recorded as act 21 somewhere «…a Vico». The bride's father reads **Gaspare** rather than the Giuseppe first published. Note that the groom's own mother is a **VIGLIOTTA**; whether the two families are one is NOT established.

MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA, and on STRADA CAMELLARA — this archive has the household at STRADA COSTA in 1816. Either they moved, or the street is not the identifier here. He is NOT the Giuseppe Falco of the same street who declared a birth seven months later: that one is a CONTADINO married to ANTONIA DI GUIDA. Two Giuseppe Falco on one street in one year, separated by trade and by wife.
Alive and bearing a child on 18 March 1819, three days after burying two. Her age is given in this act; it is recorded rather than relied on.

HER SECOND MARRIAGE, FROM THE MARGIN OF HER OWN BIRTH ACT — a document written fifty-seven years before it. «*A 30 Dic.re 1880 l'Uf.le dello Stato Civile d'**ARIENZO** sposò **PASQUA FALCO** con **PASQUALE CARFORA*** — 27 Agosto 1881». She married **ANGELO MAJONE on 9 September 1856** at thirty-three; this makes her **fifty-seven** and, on the ordinary reading, a widow of Majone. THE ANNOTATION SITS ON ACT 38 OF 1823, her own — born 30 March 1823 to Giuseppe Falco, «*il nome di PASQUA*» — so the identification is physical rather than inferred. **CARFORA is a surname this archive hunts elsewhere** — Maria Carfora of Forchia, generation seven's grandmother, whose parents remain unreachable. **Pasquale Carfora is NOT claimed as kin to her**: the name is dense at Forchia and present at Arienzo, and nothing here joins them.
Alive and marrying at fifty-seven. This archive's latest dated sighting of her had been her first wedding in 1856.

«*il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI** [di] **Gaspare**(?)*» — from the margin of her husband's birth act. **Her father's forename was first published as Giuseppe and re-reads as GASPARE at five times magnification; neither is certain.** **And the comune is not established**: Santa Maria a Vico, the obvious candidate, is excluded by its own 1856 register, whose act 21 is a de Lucia. Nothing else about her is known.

«*l'Uf.le dello Stato Civile d'Arienzo sposò PASQUA FALCO con **PASQUALE CARFORA***» — her second husband, married when she was fifty-seven. **NOT claimed as kin to the Carfora of Forchia** whom this archive hunts elsewhere; the surname is common in both towns and nothing joins them.

THE FIRST CHILD OF THIS MARRIAGE TO BE FOUND, and the second record anywhere to name Angela Falco. Declared by Arcangelo Anigale, 48, fruttajolo, and Raffaele Rivetti, 26, contadino, as «vicino e parente». Angela is named without «fu», so she was still living in February 1819.

Declared by Nicola Maggione and Alessandro Martone, both twenty-two and both «vicino della defunta». HER PARENTAGE EXPLAINS THE 1816 ACT: when Crescenzo died, GIOACCHINO FALCO and GIUSEPPE FALCO declared it as «parenti del defunto» — they were his wife's brothers.

Angelo at 58 in 1816 is exactly the ANGELO MORGILLO, 70, COLONO of strada Cappuccini who declares in 1828 and heads the Monticello de' Cappuccini household. So this man and the head of that house are the same, and his parents are SIMONE MORGILLO and GAETANA LAUDATO (b. c. 1738).

With the Donna Francesca Rivetti of January 1816, daughter of Don Nicola Rivetti and Donn'Anna Quotolo, he is the second sign of a Rivetti branch of standing at Arienzo. A LEAD: a Giuseppe di Guida is named in October 1817 as the father of Angelo Andrea di Guida by Michedalena Rivetti, and Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara married an ANTONIA DI GUIDA. A man of sixty-eight in 1819 is the right age to be father to both. Nothing here names Antonia, so it is not asserted.

«figlio di ARCANGELO CRISCI, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — the FIRST CIVIL RECORD to place this marriage on the ground. Until now the archive knew of Arcangelo Crisci's marriage to Anna Falco only at second hand. He is a contadino, and he lives on the family's own street.

«e di ANNA FALCO, domiciliata ivi» — alive on 24 January 1820, and bearing a child two days earlier. She is said to have died at twenty-two later in this same year, which would put her birth about 1798.

«è morto nella sua propria casa FORTUNATO CRISCI di giorni due, nato in Arienzo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — two days old. Declared by ANDREA CRISCI, 60, and MARCELLO CRISCI, 25, both contadini of strada Camellara, each «vicino del defunto». The Andrea Crisci who reported Anna Falco's namesake's death in 1831 is given as fifty-eight, which fits this man.

«ANNA FALCO di anni venticinque, moglie di ARCANGELO CRISCI … figlia di PASQUALE FALCO … e di CHIARA RIVETTI» — she is a daughter of the direct line's generation two. Declared by Giuseppe Martone, 40, and Domenico Martone, 36, both contadini of strada Camellara.

THE DATE OF A MARRIAGE THIS ARCHIVE HELD ONLY AS A FACT. The 1818 Tavola Alfabetica annuale de' Matrimonj pairs «ARCANGELO COSSI» with «ANNA FALCO», her parents given as «DI PASQUALE, e CHIARA RIVETTI» — no «fu» before either, and Pasquale Falco did not die until 1834. Married before the church 3 MAGGIO 1818. Anna was baptised 28 October 1795, so she married at TWENTY-TWO and was dead at twenty-four, on 23 August 1820. THE SURNAME IS WRITTEN COSSI HERE AND CRISCI IN THE 1820 ACTS — both read from the image, and this archive has already recorded that Cossi and Crisci are not reliably separable in this hand. The identification does not rest on it: there is one Anna Falco of Pasquale and Chiara, and one Arcangelo she was married to

This archive wrote that five earlier acts had called him «only a neighbour» and that this one was the first to state kinship. IT WAS NOT THE FIRST. The act of 25 March 1824 enters BOTH Falco declarants as «ZIO DEL DEFUNTO», and this archive transcribed that word as «vicino». CORRECTION, LEFT VISIBLE. This archive carried this household as «Francesco COSSI & Maria Falco» from 1823 to 1828. It is CIOFFI. The 1825 register, read at full resolution, writes the strada Camellara family with a dotted «i» after the C — «Cesare Cioffi», «Francesco Cioffi», «Giuseppa Cioffi» — and writes the strada Cossi family, in the same volume and the same hand, without one: «Domenico Cossi», «Crescenzo Cossi», «strada Cossi». Two different families, distinguished by the clerk and conflated by this archive. Everything else about the household stands.

A SECOND LIFE CLOSED FROM BOTH ENDS IN ONE VOLUME. «…è comparso FRANCESCO COSSI, di anni VENTISETTE, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo comune STRADA CAMELLARA, quale ci ha presentato una FEMINA … nata da MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima, di anni VENTICINQUE … nel giorno DICIOTTO del mese di GIUGNO … alle ore TRE E MEZZA, nella casa sua propria di abitazione … il nome di GIUSEPPA». Witnesses Tomaso Esposito, 46, contadino of STRADA CAMELLARA, and Antonio Bernardo, 47, NEGOZIANTE of strada Terra Murata. She died 2 April 1825 «di mesi OTTO» — from 18 June 1824 that is nine and a half months, recorded as eight, and GIUSEPPE FALCO declared her death

«è comparso ALFONSO DIGLIO, di anni TRENTADUE, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo comune STRADA CAMELLARA, quale ci ha presentato una FEMINA» — thirty-two in May 1825 gives b. c.1793. Thirty-three in May 1825 gives b. c.1792. SHE IS NOT the Maria Falco buried 24 July 1817 (daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Rosa Sossi, widow of Francesco Quotolo), NOR the Maria Falco already dead by February 1818 (wife of Nicola Majone), NOR the Maria Falco who was wife of FRANCESCO COSSI and living on 2 April 1825 — a woman cannot have two living husbands, and Francesco Cossi was alive that month. WHICH FALCO HOUSE SHE COMES FROM IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti baptised a Maria on 30 October 1790, which would make her thirty-four here rather than thirty-three; that is within this register's documented error, and it is NOT ENOUGH TO JOIN THEM

THE ONLY FALCO IN TWENTY ANNUAL REGISTERS DESCRIBED AS A POSSIDENTE, and not on strada Camellara. He carries the founding ancestor's name; nothing yet names his father. UNJOINED to this line.

«ANGELO MORGILLO, di anni SETTANTA, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in strada Cappuccini» — declaring atto 56. Born about 1758. A SECOND Angelo Morgillo, distinct from the Angelo, 58, of strada Nuova di San Gaetano buried in October 1826; the distinction resolves the age conflict raised by Saveria Morgillo's act of 1827, whose father he is very likely to be.

34 in 1828, contadino. Husband of Maria Majone; their eight-year-old Raffaele died in May (atto 14). He declares his brother's child's death as «zio della defunta» (atto 56), which makes him and Vincenzo brothers.
29 in May 1828, 32 in December. Husband of Felicetta Rivetti; their one-year-old Grazia died on 30 October, declared by his brother Nicola as «zio della defunta».

His parents, from the 1816 register: SIMONE MORGILLO and GAETANA LAUDATO, who died on 9 March 1816 aged seventy-eight, «vedova di Simone Morgillo», of strada Trave. Angelo declared it himself, aged fifty-eight — which is exactly seventy in 1828.

«GAETANA LAUDATO figlia delli fu Giacinto Laudato e Giovanna —, VEDOVA DI SIMONE MORGILLO, di anni SETTANTOTTO, contadina, domiciliata nella strada Trave» — born about 1738, the deepest this archive reaches into the Morgillo.

«GENNARO MORGILLO, vedovo di Felicia Sompone, nato in Arienzo, di anni cinquantatré, di professione COLONO, domiciliato STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di ANGELO MORGILLO defunto, di professione COLONO» — born about 1790. A THIRD SON of the colono Angelo, and the one who left the hill: he lived on strada Camellara, the Falco street. HIS DEATH WAS DECLARED BY GIUSEPPE FALCO, colono of the same street. It is the closest the record comes to the Falco-Morgillo marriage that was still thirty years away.

«figlio di GIOACCHINO CIOFFI defunto, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, E DI FRANCESCA FALCO defunta» — from the death act of her son Aniello Cioffi, 27 July 1843, verified at full resolution. Her son was seventy-six, so born about 1767, which places her marriage in the seventeen-sixties and her own birth in the seventeen-forties: the generation of MATTEO FALCO himself. NOTHING NAMES HER PARENTS and this archive does not guess at them.

A contadino, dead before July 1843. Named only in his son's death act. Note the forename: a GIOACCHINO FALCO, thirty-six, declares on strada Camellara in 1816 and is a candidate fifth child of Matteo Falco — the name runs in both houses, which is suggestive and nothing more.
«ANIELLO CIOFFI, marito di Giovanna Laudato, nato in Arienzo, di anni SETTANTASEI, contadino» — born about 1767, the same year as Pasquale Falco of generation two.

«figlio di MICHELE FALCO, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi» — from the death act of his two-year-old son Matteo Falco, Arienzo Morti 1842 atto 55, 25 August 1842, read at 2800px. Named WITHOUT «fu», so alive. A contadino on strada Camellara, the street of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti. NO ACT NAMES HIS PARENTS. He is not placed in the line here, and the archive will not place him until an act does.
«e di ANTONIA MIGLIORE, domiciliata ivi» — same act, also without «fu», so alive in 1842. Migliore is a common Arienzo surname and no parents are named for her.

«è morto nella sua propria casa MATTEO FALCO D'ANNI DUE, nato in Arienzo» — died at ten at night on 24 August 1842, aged two, so born about 1840. HIS NAME IS THE QUESTION. Neapolitan custom named a first son for his father's father, and the name at the head of this line is MATTEO FALCO, who married Francesca Crisci. That is a reason to look for Michele among Matteo's sons. IT IS NOT EVIDENCE. A naming habit is not a record, and this archive does not build a generation out of one.

Forty-seven, a contadino of strada Camellara. THIRTEEN MONTHS LATER, at forty-eight, the same man reports the death of CHIARA RIVETTI on the same street. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco four different ages, this one holds. He is a neighbour; the act does not call him kin, and these registers write «parente» when they mean it.
Thirty-two, a contadino of strada Camellara — a further Cioffi on the Falco street, alongside Vincenzo Cioffi the vinivendolo (atto 41), Luca Cioffi the sartore and Giovanni Cioffi (1843).

Named in THREE acts, all without «fu», so alive throughout: Morti 1840 atto 50 (17 Aug 1840), Morti 1842 atto 2 (2 Jan 1842) and Morti 1843 atto 17 (10 Jun 1843). The 1843 act was read at strip resolution and published as «DOMENICA Falco» — explicitly flagged at the time as a hypothesis, not a finding. The 1840 and 1842 acts, both read at 2600–2800px, give FRANCESCA. The correction stands beside the error in the notes rather than replacing it. NO ACT NAMES HER PARENTS, and the archive does not guess at them. She is NOT the older Francesca Falco who married Gioacchino Cioffi and whose son died at seventy-six in 1843 — that woman was born in the 1740s; this one is bearing children in 1840. Two women, two generations apart, each married to a Cioffi.
A contadino of strada Cioffi, named without «fu» in all three acts. He appears in person as a declarant in Morti 1842 atto 80, aged THIRTY-SIX, which would put his birth about 1806.
«È morta nella sua propria casa MADDALENA CIOFFI D'UN ANNO.» One year old. The earliest of the three acts.
«È morto nella sua propria casa LUIGI CIOFFI DI UN GIORNO.» One day old.
Seventeen days old. This is the act whose mother's name the archive first misread; see Francesca Falco above.

A contadino of STRADA CAMELLARA — the street of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti. He is one of the two men who report CHIARA RIVETTI'S DEATH on 13 September 1843. He declares on that street across four volumes, and his stated age is, after the first entry, the steadiest series in these registers: FORTY in 1840, FORTY-SEVEN in August 1842, FORTY-EIGHT in September 1843. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco eleven different ages, this clerk got one right. HE IS A NEIGHBOUR. No act calls him kin to the Falco, and these registers write «parente» when they mean it.
Named without «fu» in the death act of their infant daughter, so alive in November 1840. Nothing else in these registers names her.
«È morta nella sua propria casa MARTA CIOFFI D'UN MESE.» One month old. Declared by Clemente Cioffi and Virgilio Cioffi, both of strada Camellara — a fourth and fifth Cioffi on the Falco street.

A POSSIDENTE, dead before 1840. Named in two death acts a generation apart, with the same rank and trade both times: as father of MARIA GIUSEPPA SCARPATI (Morti 1840 atto 28) and as father of DON ANGELO SCARPATI, ARCIPRETE OF ARIENZO (Morti 1842 atto 15).

THE ONE DISCREPANCY, AND IT IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. The 1840 act names the mother SERAFINA Cimmino; the 1842 act names her FAUSTINA Cimmino. Same surname, same rank, same husband's name and trade, children born about 1766 and 1768. Either a clerk misread a forename, or Stefano Scarpati married twice. The archive records both readings and joins the two children as a STRONG INFERENCE, not a proven sibling pair.

Seventy-two, «DI PROFESSIONE SORORA DEL CONSERVATORIO», died «NEL CONSERVATORIO DI SAN FILIPPO [NERI]» — a SECOND religious house in Arienzo, distinct from the Ave Gratia Plena where every other institutional death in these registers happens. Atto 46 of the same volume names a STRADA SAN FILIPPO NERI, which corroborates the dedication from the other direction. Born about 1768.

Seventy-six, «DI PROFESSIONE ARCIPRETE» — the archpriest of Arienzo, born about 1766. This archive has been reading Latin parish burial entries from Arienzo for months; the man who presided over the parish through most of that period now has a name, an age and a family. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH is that he wrote any particular entry: an archpriest presides, curates write. Chiara Rivetti's 1843 burial entry was made after his death.

e morta nel Monastero d'Ave Gratia Plena, Donna Raffaela de Falco, d'anni sessantasette … monaca … figlia di Don Francesco Falco defunto, di professione proprietario — b. c. 1769. A gentry branch; no connection to the documented line established

members.evidence: THE MARRIAGE, FOUND — this archive held the household from its children alone. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO**, di anni **trentaquattro**, nato in **FORCHIA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in **FORCHIA**, figlio di **fu CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, di professione contadino, e di **fu ROSA CEGLIA** … e **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA**, di anni **ventinove**, nata in **ARIENZO**, domiciliata in Arienzo, figlia di **fu [?]ERIO CARFORA**, di professione contadino, e di **fu PASQUA MORGILLO***». Witnesses **Pasquale Laudato** and a **di Antonio Crispi**. Their first known child, Maria Rosa, was born 7 March 1861 — thirteen months later.

SABATINO'S FATHER, AND A GENERATION THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. «*figlio di **fu CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, di professione **contadino***» — dead before January 1860, of Forchia. **NOT the Carmine Annecchino who married Maria Carfora and fathered Filomena in 1897**; that one was bearing children from 1883 and is two generations later. **The name recurs in this family**, which is worth holding onto rather than resolving.
«*e di **fu ROSA CEGLIA***» — Sabatino Annecchino's mother, dead before January 1860. **CEGLIA HAS NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE**, under any spelling.

«*MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA, di anni **ventinove**, **nata in ARIENZO***» — so born about 1831, and **an Arienzo woman, not a Forchia one**. This archive had her only as a mother of four daughters born 1861–1866.

THE ACT THAT JOINS TWO HOUSEHOLDS THIS ARCHIVE KEPT APART. «*sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale **MICHELE FALCO maggiore, di anni QUARANTATRE, nato in ARIENZO, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in STRADA CAMELLARA, figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO DEFUNTO**, di professione simile, domiciliato ivi, e di **CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**, di professione filatrice … **VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI** … e **GIOVANNA D'AMBROGIO maggiore, di anni DICIANNOVE**, di professione contadina*». **«Michele Falco & Antonia Vigliotta» and «Michele Falco & Maria Giovanna d'Ambrogio» are ONE MAN AND TWO MARRIAGES.** The d'Ambrogio household was known only by a daughter **Antonia born 19 November 1850** — nine months after this wedding.

«*VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI*» — she was dead by 12 February 1850. Her daughter Chiara died in 1846 aged seven and her daughter Carmela on 4 August 1859, which is AFTER this date and therefore a child of the first marriage buried nine years into the second.

MICHELE FALCO'S FATHER, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME: «*figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO DEFUNTO**, di professione **simile** [colono], domiciliato **ivi** [strada Camellara]*». A generation this archive did not have for this house. NOT joined to the direct line's Raffaele Falco of 1818, who was thirty-one and alive in 1850.

«*e di **CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**, di professione **filatrice***». **A NAME THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAS, AND THIS IS ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT HER.** Generation two's wife CHIARA RIVETTI was the widow of **PASQUALE** Falco, died 13 September 1843 aged eighty, and bore Pasquale children from 1789 to 1802 — so she cannot have been married to a Raffaele Falco when this Michele was born about 1807. **Either a second Chiara Rivetti, on a street where the Rivetti are dense, or Michele's stated age is badly wrong. Nothing is merged and nothing is chosen.**

«*è comparso **ANIELLO CARFORA**, di anni **trentuno**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in questo Comune **STRADA CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato un **Maschio***» — atto of 10 January 1831. **A CARFORA HOUSEHOLD ON THE FALCO'S OWN STREET**, thirty years before the marriage act that first told this archive the Carfora were an Arienzo family at all. Thirty-one here, so born about 1800 — the same generation as «[?]erio Carfora», Maria Antonia's father. **He is not that man**: this one's wife is Orsola Porrino. THIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOT JOINED TO ANY OTHER IN THIS ARCHIVE. It is recorded because work-list row 63 asked whether the Carfora were an Arienzo family at all, and the answer is that they were — three separate Carfora households appear in a single year of one register. Whether any of them is the house of «[?]erio Carfora and Pasqua Morgillo» is NOT established and is not claimed.

members.evidence:
**READ THE ARITHMETIC OF THIS ACT BEFORE USING IT.** It names **four** surviving children, aged **fifteen, twelve, ten and five**, and it makes their father **fifty-three**. A man of fifty-three whose eldest living child is fifteen either married at thirty-eight or **has older children who are not on this list** — and these acts list the children who need a tutor, which is to say the minors. **So this is not a complete list of his children and must not be read as one.**

**IT BEARS ON ALESSANDRA CRISCI.** She married **MATTEO FALCO** on 24 January 1834, and the marriage index gives her parents as «*CRISCI [forename lost to the fold shadow], [QUO]TOLO ANGELA*». This archive filed that as **a resemblance and not a fact**, because Angela Quotolo is not a rare name here and the father's forename cannot be read — **and that still stands.** What this act removes is the obvious objection to it: that Alessandra is not among his children. **She would not be, if she was already grown.** A resemblance with a hole in it is now a resemblance without one, and it is still not a fact.
